historical_record.description: The Recreation and Park Commission approved schematic designs for a children's play area at Chinese Playground by Eckbo, Dean, Austin and Williams, who gave their design services; the work was paid for by an anonymous $20,000 gift with matching federal grant money, after three years' effort by the Committee for Better Parks and Recreation in Chinatown.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved an architect's agreement with EDAW, Inc. to design a recreation building and improvements at Chinese Playground, for a fee of $19,500; EDAW had done the siting and preliminary design in the summer.
The second phase of improvements at Chinese Playground officially began on June 7, as the general manager reported to the Recreation and Park Commission.

Reporting the construction contract for the new recreation building at Chinese Playground as awarded, $290,000 for the building and $49,000 for improvements to the middle terrace, the Recreation and Park Commission adjusted the fee of EDAW, Inc., its architects, for a 21.6 percent rise in building costs.

The new recreation center, basketball court and small children's play area at Chinese Playground were dedicated on March 8, 1980, when Mayor Dianne Feinstein cut the ribbon for the Oliver C. Chang Recreation Building, named for the city's first recreation director of Chinese ancestry.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved a $150,000 rebuilding of Hang Ah Alley, between Sacramento and Clay beside the Chinese Playground and last improved in 1983: new trees, benches and bollards and exposed-aggregate paving with bands inscribed in English and Chinese on the alley's history, sponsored by the Chinatown Resource Center.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved a conceptual plan to rebuild the play area at Chinese Playground, with separate areas for older and younger children, a climbing wall at the west end, a maze in the paving between them, and a mural proposed for the retaining wall.
The Playground Commission bought the land for the Chinese Playground, between Sacramento and Clay Streets off Waverly Place.
